draft.title: The Reserve Bank of Australia
card: The Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) is Australia's central bank. It is owned by the nation, not by a private company.
Monetary policy means using interest rates to influence how much people and businesses spend. The RBA's Monetary Policy Board makes these decisions.
The Board makes its decisions independently of the government. This means elected politicians do not tell it what to decide.
The RBA's aims are to keep prices stable and to support full employment, which means most people who want a job can find one.
draft.remember: The RBA is the central bank. It sets monetary policy on its own, to keep prices stable and support jobs.

opts: The Prime Minister and the cabinet
a.why: The RBA's Monetary Policy Board makes monetary policy decisions. The Prime Minister and the Treasurer lead the government, but the Board decides independently of them.
a.clue: Think about which body is independent of the government.

b.q: A minister says the RBA must follow the government's wishes on interest rates before an election. Why would this go against how the RBA works?
opts: The RBA decides monetary policy independently
The RBA has no power over interest rates
The RBA only looks after the banks' profits
The RBA only handles the government's budget
b.why: The Monetary Policy Board sets monetary policy independently of the government, so the government does not direct its decisions. The RBA's aims are stable prices and full employment, not the government's budget or bank profits.
b.clue: Look at the third card line.

b.best: The RBA decides monetary policy independently
